title: Account Access
subtitle: Install it. Ask your agent. See the results.
narration: This is Account Access. In this walkthrough, we'll install it and use it with Codex and Claude Code. Everything you see uses fictional demo accounts, with no personal passwords required.

title: Start with your usual tools
subtitle: Open Terminal on your Mac. The command guide is linked below the video.
cards: Codex or Claude Code, already installed
narration: You'll need Git, the u v package manager, and your preferred AI agent already installed and signed in. The written guide links to u v installation. This video uses a Mac; Linux has extra browser setup instructions.
note: No AI API key is needed for the demo. Native Windows support is not shipped.

title: Download Account Access
subtitle: Copy these commands into Terminal, one line at a time.
output:
Cloning into 'account-access'...
Download complete. You are now inside the project folder.
narration: First, clone the public GitHub repository. Then change into the account access folder. All installation commands in the next steps run from this folder.
tip: The written guide includes every command, ready to copy.
note: Commands and successful output are presented for clarity; installation waits are shortened.

title: Install Python and the browser
subtitle: Wait for each command to finish before running the next.
command:
uv sync --locked --python 3.13
uv run playwright install chromium
uv build
narration: Run these three commands. The first prepares Python and the dependencies. The second installs the browser used by website connectors. The third builds the installable package. The first run can take a few minutes.
tip: Linux: use the browser dependency instructions in docs/setup.md.
note: Fresh checkout installation verified on 13 October 2026. Output abridged.

title: Make the command available
subtitle: The backslash continues the command onto the next line.
narration: Install the package as a command line tool. If your terminal cannot find account access afterward, run u v tool update shell and open a new terminal. The guide also covers a missing Python three launcher.
tip:
If the command is missing:
uv tool update-shell
Then open a new terminal.
note: This installs the service and CLI. The next step installs the agent skill.

title: Start it once. Keep it running.
subtitle: This terminal becomes the local service. Leave it open while you use the demo.
output:
environment: controlled-demo
Skills installed: Codex + Claude Code
Demo accounts: demo-api, demo-web, demo-mfa
Keep this process running while testing agents.
narration: Start the demo with this command. It prepares three fictional accounts and installs the Account Access skill for both Codex and Claude Code. Keep this terminal open. The demo handles its test credentials and authenticator code automatically.
tip:
Three synthetic accounts:
OAuth API
Password website
Password + authenticator
note: Demo data stays in its own directory. Never point this command at a real-account vault.

title: Check the connection
subtitle: Open a second terminal. Keep the service running in the first one.
narration: In a second terminal, run the connection check. Look for status O K and service reachable true. That confirms the installed client can reach the local demo service.
tip:
service_unavailable?
Start the demo again and keep its terminal open.
note: Actual service response, abridged. This check does not read private accounts.

title: Ask Codex in a fresh chat
subtitle: The dollar sign selects the installed skill.
prompt: Use $account-access to read one permitted operation from every connected demo account. Save progress as a task and label the results as demo data.
narration: Open a fresh Codex chat and paste this prompt. Codex discovers the accounts, creates a task, waits for it, and reports the results. Our actual Codex command line run completed all three reads. You don't type the demo password or code.
note: Suggested chat prompt shown. Result highlights come from a verified Codex CLI run.

title: The same service works with Claude
subtitle: Start a fresh Claude Code session. Select the skill with a slash.
prompt: /account-access Read one permitted operation from every connected demo account, save progress as a task, and label the results as demo data.
narration: In Claude Code, start a fresh session and use slash account access with the same request. The service is shared, while each agent has its own client identity. This actual Claude Code run also completed all three demo reads.
note: Suggested session prompt shown. Result highlights come from a verified Claude Code CLI run.

title: You choose the account and permissions
subtitle: Actual owner console, showing synthetic accounts.
narration: For a real account, a reviewed connector must exist first. Then owner setup lets you enter credentials locally, connect or repair the account, and choose the operations an agent may perform. The demo has already prepared its accounts and permissions for you.
note: Real accounts: initialize a reviewed configuration, serve it, then open account-access setup.

title: Where authentication comes from
subtitle: Configure supported sources once. Reuse saved sessions afterward.
narration: Today, passwords are entered once in local setup. An enrolled authenticator secret lets the service generate login codes. Gmail and Twilio adapters exist, but live code delivery is not validated. Personal phone inbox access and password manager import are not built yet.
note: Provider-required fingerprint, passkey, device or admin approval still needs the owner.

title: Follow the specific status
subtitle: A task preserves its progress when authentication needs repair.
narration: If the skill is missing, open a fresh agent session. If the service is unavailable, restart it. Needs user means complete the specified step in owner setup, then continue the same task. Denied means review the permissions you granted.
note: The service must remain running, and your computer must stay awake.

title: Your first three-account task
subtitle: Install → start the demo → ask your agent.
narration: You're ready to try the three account demo. The repository has every command, the captioned video, and the real account setup guide. This is a release candidate; arbitrary websites, banks, and insurance accounts still require connectors and testing.
